title: Abelian groups admit functorial flat resolutions
statement: For every universe $\mathcal U$, give the category $\operatorname{Ab}_{\mathcal U}$ of $\mathcal U$-small abelian groups its tensor product over $\mathbf Z$, with unit $\mathbf Z$ and internal hom the group of homomorphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Call an object flat if tensoring with it on either side preserves short exact sequences. There is a functor $P:\operatorname{Ab}_{\mathcal U}\to\operatorname{Ab}_{\mathcal U}$ with flat values and a natural transformation $\pi:P\to\operatorname{id}$ such that every $\pi_M$ is an epimorphism. Thus this category admits functorial flat resolutions in the sense of [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution].

source.place: Part 4, free abelian flat covers; coefficient input to the sheaf construction. Project declaration AddCommGrpCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution, WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/ModuleObject/Basic.lean:148-152; its instance is constructed in WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/RingObjects/Ab.lean:289-291.

proof.text: Fix $\mathcal U$. For an abelian group $M$, let $P(M)=\bigoplus_{m\in |M|}\mathbf Z$, concretely the finitely supported integer-valued functions on the underlying set of $M$, with pointwise addition. Write $e_m$ for the function equal to $1$ at $m$ and $0$ elsewhere. Each element has the unique expression $\sum_m a_m e_m$ given by its coordinates, so $(e_m)_{m\in |M|}$ is a basis by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. This construction stays in $\mathcal U$. For a homomorphism $f:M\to N$ define $P(f)(\sum_m a_m e_m)=\sum_m a_m e_{f(m)}$. The sum is finite; repeated indices are added, and distributivity makes this an additive homomorphism. Both $P(\mathrm{id}_M)$ and the identity send $e_m$ to $e_m$, while $P(g\circ f)$ and $P(g)\circ P(f)$ send $e_m$ to $e_{g(f(m))}$. Additivity and the displayed expression give equality on every element. Thus $P$ is a functor.

source.place: Part 4, canonical free abelian cover: coefficient version on underlying sets; finite-sum construction written out by NH (Stacks Tag 00C2, algebra-item-free-module, for the basis convention)

proof.text: Define $\pi_M:P(M)\to M$ by $\pi_M(\sum_m a_m e_m)=\sum_m a_m m$, where integers act by repeated addition and negatives. Finite-sum distributivity proves additivity. For $f:M\to N$, additivity gives $f(\sum_m a_m m)=\sum_m a_m f(m)$, so $f\circ\pi_M=\pi_N\circ P(f)$ on every element. Hence $\pi:P\to\mathrm{id}$ is natural. Since $\pi_M(e_m)=m$, each $\pi_M$ is surjective. It is also an epimorphism: if $a,b:M\to T$ satisfy $a\circ\pi_M=b\circ\pi_M$, evaluate on $e_m$ to get $a(m)=b(m)$ for every $m$, whence $a=b$. No additive structure on the functor $P$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Part 4, sentence: the canonical map is a functorial epimorphism; coefficient finite-sum and cancellation argument written out by NH

proof.text: The canonical integer action makes every abelian group a $\mathbf Z$-module, and every additive homomorphism is $\mathbf Z$-linear (the positive integer case follows by induction on repeated addition, and the negative case by preservation of negatives). The basis in step 1 makes $P(M)$ a free $\mathbf Z$-module. Apply the free-module clause of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] with $R=\mathbf Z$: $P(M)$ is flat as a module, without a finite-rank hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 051G, algebra-lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat, opening sentence of the proof: every projective module is flat and every free module is projective; the cited node isolates this unrestricted fact

proof.text: Take a short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ of abelian groups. It is the same short exact sequence of $\mathbf Z$-modules: kernels are the subgroups mapping to zero and cokernels are quotients by image, with their inherited integer actions. For the flat module $P(M)$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] gives injectivity of the first tensored map and exactness at the middle, for tensoring on either side. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to $A\to B\to C\to0$ to obtain surjectivity of the last tensored map, again on either side. These are exactly the three conditions for a short exact sequence. The tensors here are precisely those specified for $\operatorname{Ab}_{\mathcal U}$ in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], namely $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$, so $P(M)$ is flat in the sense of the item.

source.place: Tags 00HD (algebra-lemma-flat) and 00DF (algebra-lemma-tensor-product-exact): flat tensor preserves exactness and tensor is right exact

proof.text: Steps 1 and 4 give a functor with flat values, and step 2 gives a natural transformation to the identity whose components are epimorphisms. This is exactly the meaning of functorial flat resolution stated in [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution]. The universe was arbitrary, so the assertion holds for every $\mathcal U$.
